title: Candlestick Patterns
summary: Labels fifteen classic one, two and three bar candlestick patterns, from dojis and hammers to engulfings, kickers and morning and evening stars.
description:
Candlestick Patterns tests every bar for fifteen patterns and labels each one it finds. Bullish patterns are marked with a green arrow below the bar, bearish ones with a red arrow above it, and neutral ones in white.

- **Doji**: the body is at most `Doji size` of the bar's range.
- **Harami** (bullish and bearish): a body that sits inside the previous bar's body, in the opposite colour.
- **Engulfing** (bullish and bearish): a body that covers the previous bar's body, in the opposite colour.
- **Piercing Line**: after a down bar, a gap below its low that closes back above the middle of its body.
- **Bullish Belt**: a bar that opens on its low, below the lowest low of the previous ten bars, and closes up.
- **Kicker** (bullish and bearish): a bar that opens beyond the previous bar's open and runs the other way.
- **Hanging Man**, **Shooting Star**, **Hammer** (H) and **Inverted Hammer** (IH): small bodies at one end of a long range.
- **Morning Star** and **Evening Star**: three bars where a small middle bar gaps away and the third bar reverses.

The harami, engulfing, piercing, belt, kicker and hanging man patterns also require a prior move: the open `Trend in Bars` bars ago must be above the current open for a bullish pattern and below it for a bearish one.
howToRead:
Treat each label as a description of what the last bars did, not as an instruction. A reversal pattern matters most where a move is stretched and the pattern forms at a level you already watch, such as a prior high or low; the same pattern in the middle of a range means little.

Look for confirmation from the next bar: a bullish engulfing followed by a higher close says more than the engulfing alone. On a busy chart several patterns can mark the same bar, because the definitions overlap (a hammer can also be a hanging man, depending on the trend before it).

settings.label: Trend in Bars
settings.description: How many bars back the open is compared with, to require a prior move before a reversal pattern counts.

settings.label: Doji size
settings.description: The largest body, as a fraction of the bar's range, that still counts as a doji.

settings.label: Bullish Arrow Color
settings.description: Colour of the arrows and labels for bullish patterns.

settings.label: Bearish Arrow Color
settings.description: Colour of the arrows and labels for bearish patterns.

settings.label: Other (Doji) Symbol Color
settings.description: Colour of the doji, hammer and inverted hammer marks.

faq.q: Why do some bars carry more than one label?
faq.a: The definitions overlap. A bar with a small body near its high can be a hammer and a hanging man, and a doji can also meet another pattern's rules, so each pattern that holds is marked.

faq.q: What does Trend in Bars do?
faq.a: It asks for a move before the pattern: for a bullish pattern the open that many bars ago must be above the current open, so the pattern comes after a decline. A larger value looks further back.

faq.q: Can I be alerted to a pattern?
faq.a: Yes. Each of the fifteen patterns has its own alert, raised on the bar it forms.
